C0.quote: study equilibrium behavior under alternative majority rules
C0.note: Repeated majority voting in committees; equilibrium analysis of voting rule.

C1.quote: characterizes the set of equilibrium payoffs and the optimal consensus probability
C1.note: Equilibrium payoffs characterisation dominates; welfare comparison of majority rules (WD); SB included because of strategic non-sincere voting incentives (judgement call).

C2.1.quote: each agent i votes either in favor or against the reform

C2.2.quote: A voting strategy vi for player i associates to any reform u a vote vi (u) ∈ {0, 1}
C2.2.note: Binary vote in favour/against a reform; not rankings/approval sets of candidates.

C2.3.quote: the reform yields utility ui ∈ R to agent i ∈ N

C2.4.quote: agents sometimes voting against their immediate preference
C2.4.note: Votes and utilities are separate objects, and votes may differ from preferences.

C3.1.quote: every agent votes sincerely, i.e. vi (u) = 1{ui ≥ 0}
C3.1.note: Stage game analysis is sincere (weakly undominated equilibrium); repeated game involves non-sincere voting as equilibrium.

C3.2.quote: voting sincerely is a weakly dominant strategy
C3.2.note: Static benchmark sincerity stated in words.

C3.3.quote: sincere voting is a dominant strategy and the collective decision coincides
C3.3.note: Reason: dominance in the static binary decision.

C4.1.note: Input is binary vote; cardinal utilities are primitives; no RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR format.

C5.1.quote: the efficient rule de (.) accepts every good reform and rejects every bad reform
C5.1.note: Efficiency and utilitarian welfare U(d) used in results.

C5.2.note: Welfare evaluated on cardinal utilities defined separately from votes.

VOT.quote_behav: every agent votes sincerely, i.e. vi (u) = 1{ui ≥ 0}
VOT.quote_info: The reform u is publicly observed, then agents simultaneously vote
VOT.note: Sincere in stage game, strategic in repeated game equilibrium (subgame perfect). Complete info on current-stage utilities.

CAN.note: Reforms are alternatives drawn exogenously; no acting proponents.

DES.note: Optimal voting rule is evaluated by the authors, but no designer agent with explicit choice is modelled.

C8.1.quote: We focus on subgame perfect equilibria that satisfy the following three assumptions.
C8.1.note: Stage game Nash in undominated strategies; repeated game SPE.

the inefficiency of (super-) majority rules may be exaggerated by standard voting models
provides a possible explanation for the widespread observation that committee decisions

C9.1.note: Claims about real committees and rule choice.

C9.2.quote: Our model assumes complete information in the stage-game
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions (cardinal utilities, complete info, equilibrium selection/anonymous histories, independence) are stated and discussed in Sections 4 and 8.

C10.1.note: No procedural-only reading; utilities explicitly modelled.
